title: Flat scalar extension of derived Hom from a pseudo-coherent complex
statement:
Let $R\to S$ be a flat homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Work in the ordinary derived categories of modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], regarded as sheaves on the one-object site with trivial topology, so $R\operatorname{Hom}$ is [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and extension of scalars is [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $E\in D(R)$ be pseudo-coherent, meaning isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free $R$-modules [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], and let $L\in D^+(R)$, meaning $H^i(L)=0$ for all sufficiently negative integers $i$. The canonical derived-Hom scalar-extension map
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_R(E,L)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_S(E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S,L\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(S)$, natural in $E$ and $L$. The map is the adjoint, under extension and restriction of scalars, of the map obtained by applying extension of scalars to morphisms and using its unit $L\to L\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S$. No perfectness of $E$ and no Noetherian hypothesis on either ring is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0A6A (lemma-base-change-RHom), clause (3), including the map of Equation 0E1X and the comparison of Tag 0E1W.

proof.text: Choose integers $a,b$ and representatives $E\simeq Q_RP$, $L\simeq Q_RN$, with $P^p=0$ for $p>b$, every $P^p$ finite free, and $N^q=0$ for $q<a$. The first choice is exactly [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]; the second follows from the equivalence in [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] between cohomological and representative lower bounds. A free module is projective: lift the images of its basis vectors through any surjection and extend linearly. Write $F(C)=C\otimes_R S$ termwise; in formulas we write $s\otimes x$ for $x\otimes s$ using the canonical tensor swap, whose inverse swaps back. Write and $Q_R,Q_S$ for localization into the corresponding derived categories.

source.place: Tag 0ATK, lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-tensor-isomorphism, proof of (3), with K=S concentrated in degree zero; Tag 064P for pseudo-coherence

proof.text: Flatness makes $F$ exact by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. More explicitly, for any complex $C$ put $Z^i=\ker d_C^i$ and $B^i=\operatorname{im}d_C^{i-1}$. Applying exact tensor to $0\to Z^i\to C^i\to B^{i+1}\to0$ and $0\to B^i\to Z^i\to H^i(C)\to0$ identifies the cycles and boundaries of $F(C)$ with $F(Z^i)$ and $F(B^i)$, and gives $H^i(F(C))\cong S\otimes_RH^i(C)$. The identifications commute with chain maps, so $F$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms. This argument has no boundedness hypothesis on $C$.

source.place: Tag 0A6A(3), flatness reduction; exactness of flat tensor: algebra.tex, lemma-flat (Tag 00HD)

proof.text: For any $C$, choose a K-flat resolution $K\to C$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], $LF(Q_RC)$ is canonically represented by $F(K)$. Step 2 makes $F(K)\to F(C)$ a quasi-isomorphism, hence gives the natural comparison $LF(Q_RC)\simeq Q_SF(C)$, for arbitrary $C$, including the Hom complex used below. These comparisons respect the resolution comparisons of the cited theorem. The extension/restriction adjunction exists by [lem-sc-mixed-global-extension-adjunction]. Its unit is represented here by $c\mapsto1\otimes c$: restriction is termwise exact, both functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms, and the ordinary unit and counit $s\otimes y\mapsto sy$ descend with their triangle identities. Thus they give the stated derived adjunction and its unit under the canonical comparisons.

source.place: Tag 0A6A(3), exact scalar extension; lemma-tensor-hom-adjoint and Equation 0E1X; K-flat existence/computation: sites-cohomology.tex, Tag 06YS

proof.text: Put $H=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P,N)$ and $H'=\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(FP,FN)$. By [lem-pod-projective-hom-evaluation-model], $Q_RH$ represents $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(E,L)$, naturally in the representatives. The terms of $FP$ are finite free over $S$ (the tensors of a basis form a basis), and it is bounded above by $b$. The same theorem over $S$ therefore identifies $Q_SH'$ with $R\operatorname{Hom}_S(LFE,LFL)$, using Step 3 for $P,N$. The product terms and differentials here are precisely those of [def-pur-hom-complex]: on the one-object site the formula is the ordinary module product-total Hom formula. These models also apply with target $\operatorname{Res}(FN)$, since the cited projective-Hom theorem permits any target complex.

source.place: Tag 0A66, lemma-RHom-out-of-projective; Tag 0ATK(3), explicit Hom models

proof.text: Use the actual scalar-extension functor as $F$ in [lem-pc-normalized-ring-hom-extension]. This gives a chain map $\chi:F(H)\to H'$ with degree-$n$ formula $\chi(s\otimes f)_p(t\otimes x)=st\otimes f_p(x)$. The object equalities required there are the scalar-extension object identifications themselves. In particular its Hom projections and pure-tensor normalization agree with the extension data of [def-pc-perfect-rhom-base-change-map]. We use only the chain-map/extension-data part of that definition, not its perfect-source derived comparison.

source.place: Equation 0E1X and Tag 0A6A; explicit normalized comparison used in Tag 0ATK(3)

proof.text: Fix $n$ and set $c=a-n$. Let $P_c=\sigma_{\ge c}P$, the stupid truncation of [def-kun-truncations]. It is bounded with finite free, hence finite projective, terms. By [def-pur-hom-complex], restriction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_R^n(P,N)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_R^n(P_c,N)$: all removed factors have $p<c$, hence $N^{p+n}=0$. The inverse inserts zero components. The identical statement holds over $S$, because $(FN)^q=0$ for $q<a$. Under these degree-$n$ identifications $\chi_n$ is exactly the degree-$n$ comparison for $P_c,N$, by the projection formula of Step 5. That comparison is an isomorphism by [lem-pc-perfect-ring-hom-scalar-extension], whose source $P_c$ is bounded finite projective; it requires neither K-flatness of $N$ nor additional ring hypotheses. Therefore every $\chi_n$ is invertible. Their inverses form a chain map by rearranging $\chi_{n+1}d=d\chi_n$, so $\chi$ is an isomorphism of complexes. The truncation depends on $n$ only for this degreewise verification; it is never substituted for $E$ in the derived category.

source.place: Tag 0ATK(3), finite-support Hom calculation, specialized to K=S[0]; bounded comparison: Tag 0A6A(1)

proof.text: We verify that $Q_S\chi$, under Steps 3--4, is the map in the statement. At the complex level the extension/restriction Hom identification sends an $S$-linear family $g_p:S\otimes P^p\to(FN)^{p+n}$ to $x\mapsto g_p(1\otimes x)$; its inverse sends $h_p$ to $(t\otimes x\mapsto t h_p(x))$. These formulas are inverse and commute with $d_Nf-(-1)^nfd_P$. Applying [lem-pod-projective-hom-evaluation-model] over $R$ to $P,\operatorname{Res}(FN)$ and over $S$ to $FP,FN$ therefore gives the derived internal-Hom identification of Tag 0E1W in these models. Applying Hom to the unit $N\to\operatorname{Res}(FN)$ gives $f_p\mapsto(x\mapsto1\otimes f_p(x))$. Its image under the inverse identification is $f_p\mapsto(t\otimes x\mapsto t\otimes f_p(x))$. By the extension/restriction adjunction [lem-sc-mixed-global-extension-adjunction], whose unit was identified in Step 3, the $S$-linear adjoint is $s\otimes f_p\mapsto(t\otimes x\mapsto st\otimes f_p(x))$. This is exactly the normalized map of [lem-pc-normalized-ring-hom-extension]. Thus Step 6 proves the required canonical map invertible. Naturality in $E,L$ follows from the functorial unit, Hom, and adjunction construction of this canonical map (all comparisons above are natural); it consequently holds for arbitrary derived morphisms, not just chain maps of the chosen representatives.
